label: Kitchen
description: The communal kettle, and the company's most reliable communications channel.

result.title: Kitchen
result.body: You wait four minutes for the kettle beside someone from Accounts Payable. You agree that it is nearly Friday. It is Tuesday.

moreResults.title: Kitchen
moreResults.body: A note on the fridge says, in capitals, that whoever keeps taking the yoghurt marked DAVE knows who they are. A second note, in different handwriting, says that so does Dave. You move your sandwich to your desk.

moreResults.title: Kitchen
moreResults.body: The dishwasher has been out of order since February. There is now a working group, and it meets in here, and you have just been asked to take notes.

moreResults.title: Kitchen
moreResults.body: Someone has brought in a cake for a colleague's leaving do. Nobody knows who is leaving. You have a slice, and sign the card.

moreResults.title: Kitchen
moreResults.body: You and a man from Facilities watch the kettle in silence. You part on good terms. It is the most honest exchange you have had this month.

moreResults.title: Kitchen
moreResults.body: The mugs have been counted, and an email is on its way. You put yours back and hold it there for a moment, in case anyone is looking.

moreResults.title: Kitchen
moreResults.body: Someone has put up a sign about the sign about the microwave. You read both, and take your soup back upstairs cold.

moreResults.title: Kitchen
moreResults.body: A person from another floor asks you whether this kitchen is always this quiet. You say that it depends. They write that down, and leave.

moreResults.title: Kitchen
moreResults.body: The good teabags are in a locked drawer now. Everyone knows who has the key, and nobody has said so. You have the other kind, and hold it up to the light.

label: The Senior Analyst's desk
description: A one-to-one, which is a conversation that can be logged.

result.title: One-to-one
result.body: You ask the Senior Analyst how things are going. You are told, at length, about the car park. You may now log this as a one-to-one.

moreResults.title: One-to-one
moreResults.body: The Senior Analyst asks you how you see your career developing. You begin to answer. The Senior Analyst says that is really interesting, and asks you to close the door on your way out.

moreResults.title: One-to-one
moreResults.body: You discuss your objectives. Neither of you has a copy. You agree that they are stretching, and you log the conversation as a success.

moreResults.title: One-to-one
moreResults.body: The Senior Analyst shows you a photograph of a dog. It takes you some time to work out that it is not the Senior Analyst's dog, and that you were expected to know that.

moreResults.title: One-to-one
moreResults.body: You are told about the car park again. There has been a development. It sounds worse than last time, and you promise to keep it to yourself.

moreResults.title: One-to-one
moreResults.body: The Senior Analyst says that this has been really useful, and asks what it was that you wanted. You say that it was nothing. The Senior Analyst makes a note of that.

moreResults.title: One-to-one
moreResults.body: The Senior Analyst has moved the meeting to a walking meeting, and walks off. You catch up by the stairs. The meeting is over.

moreResults.title: One-to-one
moreResults.body: You are asked what your biggest learning has been this year. You say that it is still landing. The Senior Analyst nods, and logs it.

moreResults.title: One-to-one
moreResults.body: The Senior Analyst says that this is a safe space, and closes the laptop, and opens it again. You talk about the car park, because it is safest.

label: Your desk
description: Doing your actual job, on your actual project. It remains an option.

result.title: Your desk
result.body: You do two hours of real work on your project. It goes well, and it does not appear in any report.

moreResults.title: Your desk
moreResults.body: You fix something that has been broken for a year. Nobody notices, because now it works. You will not be able to prove that it was you.

moreResults.title: Your desk
moreResults.body: You answer eleven emails properly. Nine of them receive a reply asking you to take this offline.

moreResults.title: Your desk
moreResults.body: You write a clear page explaining how a thing works. By Friday it has been given a new title by someone else and circulated as guidance.

moreResults.title: Your desk
moreResults.body: You finish the thing that was due. You are told that the priorities changed last week, and that you should have been told.

moreResults.title: Your desk
moreResults.body: A full, quiet afternoon of real work. You are startled to find that you enjoyed it, and you tell no one.

moreResults.title: Your desk
moreResults.body: You clear the backlog. A new backlog is created for you, and it has a better name.

moreResults.title: Your desk
moreResults.body: You find the bug that everyone has been reporting as a feature. You fix it, and three people ask you to put it back.

moreResults.title: Your desk
moreResults.body: You spend a morning writing the handover note that nobody wrote for you. You read it through, and it is good. You keep it, in case.
